findings.description: The new fast-path returns max(max(0, self.min), self.max), which is always self.max (or self.min if min > max), for attempts where the exponent is below log_base(max/multiplier). Those are exactly the early attempts whose computed wait is smaller than max.
findings.rationale: Trigger: wait_exponential(multiplier=1, max=60) on attempt 1. exponent=0 < log2(60)≈5.9, so the function returns 60 instead of the expected 1. Every early retry waits the maximum, so the exponential backoff is broken. The comparison direction is inverted: the shortcut should apply when exponent is greater than or equal to the log value, where the result is capped at max.
